actionId.description: Action id from search or listing, passed as a value; not a tool name.

examples.description: Inspect the input and output schema of a terminal status tool before calling it

tools.description: List actions a page at a time, filtered by category or substring, to walk a domain; search instead to find a capability by intent. Entries omit schemas, so fetch the schema before dispatching. Ordering is stable across pages.

category.description: Exact category, e.g. terminal, worktree, forge

search.description: Substring of id, title or description

tools.description: Find actions by describing what you want to do, ranked by match. Start here, then fetch the chosen action's schema before dispatching. Results omit schemas; no match returns an empty list, not a failure.

examples.description: Find actions related to reading terminal output
Find the top 5 worktree-listing actions

tools.description: Start an AI agent in a new terminal and report where it landed. Success means the panel exists and its process is starting, not that the agent is ready; read its status for that. A missing CLI opens a setup diagnostic panel instead. Keep concurrent launches modest.

agentId.description: Agent CLI id from the agent listing. Other strings are accepted, so a bad id fails at launch, not validation.

location.description: Default "grid". "background" runs it unmounted until restored.

cwd.description: Absolute launch directory, not a worktree selector. Defaults to the worktree root.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing. Defaults to the active worktree.

prompt.description: First turn, submitted once the agent starts. Omit to leave it waiting.

handback.description: Ask the agent to end its reply to `prompt` with a Daintree marker, read back as `lastHandback`.

notify.description: When this agent next stops, Daintree types its handback summary, else its screen, into your prompt; may be missed: poll too. Agent panes and assistants only.

replyLines.description: With notify: screen lines quoted (default 40, 0 for none); with handback, up to the marker. Set, it quotes despite a summary.

waitForReply.description: Hold the call until the agent finishes; its reply comes back in `reply`.

systemPrompt.description: Appended to the agent's system prompt, at most 2000 characters, kept on resume. Claude and Codex only; others refuse it.

interactive.description: Run as a conversation the user can continue, not one non-interactive pass.

model.description: Omit for the CLI's default; set only when the user names a model. No preset needed.

presetId.description: One of the user's saved launch presets. Explicit null ignores the default preset.

activateDockOnCreate.description: Open the sidebar dock when placing the agent there.

env.description: Extra env vars merged over the inherited environment. They reach a real process: never add credentials the user has not exposed.

excludeFromPersistence.description: Hide the terminal from the saved session, listings, status reads and bulk close or kill, so it can't be polled later. For throwaway work.

removeOnExit.description: Close the panel when the agent exits, discarding its output.

agentLaunchFlags.description: Extra CLI flags for this launch, verbatim, e.g. Codex effort ["-c", "model_reasoning_effort=high"]. Bad ones fail at CLI start.

spawnedBy.description: Run-history provenance only. Leave unset over MCP.

focusPolicy.description: Focus the new panel: "auto" (default) unless the assistant owns input, "preserve" never, "take" always. Use preserve for background spawns.

requestedId.description: Panel id to create the terminal with, to correlate the launch.

force.description: Skip the CLI launchability check, so an unlaunchable CLI starts and fails instead of opening a setup diagnostic. Leave off.

name.description: Always pass a short tab title ('Claude: auth refactor') so parallel agents are told apart. Blank uses the default.

spawnStatus.description: Null on a launch, else why not: panel-limit (see panelLimit), already-launching (retry), missing-cli (setup panel opened).

tools.description: Launch several agents with one shared prompt in one call, each a single launch in its own terminal with its own notice. Results come back in order.

agentIds.description: 1-8 distinct agent ids, one terminal each.

name.description: Tab title prefix; each tab is "<name>: <agentId>".

worktreeId.description: Defaults to the active worktree.

notify.description: As on a single call: each notice carries that agent's reply.

handback.description: As on the single call, for each item.

replyLines.description: With notify: screen lines quoted (default 40, 0 for none); with handback, up to the marker. Set, it quotes despite a summary.

waitForReply.description: Hold the call until every agent finishes; each result has its `reply`.

tools.description: List every registered agent (built-in, user-defined, plugin) from the authoritative registry, launchable or not. Use before launching, and read each entry's launchability rather than assuming it. Launchability appears once each CLI's live probe finishes; the result says while that is incomplete.
Each agent CLI's current model ids and names, to turn a model the user names into an id. With none named, launch without a model.

agentId.description: One agent's models; omit for every listed agent.

examples.description: Find the id of a Codex model the user asked for by name

tools.description: List one agent's launchable presets, merged from user settings, repository preset files and CCR as the launcher does. Identity only, no env or flags; a launch can set model and flags without one. A false completeness flag means a source is loading.

agentId.description: Agent CLI id from the agent listing. Other strings are accepted, so a bad id fails at launch, not validation.

projectId.description: Project whose repository presets to include (default: this call's). Another project returns only the other layers, marked incomplete.

examples.description: Discover the preset ids available for Claude Code

tools.description: Read this machine's Codex account quota, as Codex reports it: how much of each rate-limit window is used and when it resets.

usedPercent.description: Percent of this window's limit used, 0-100.

windowDurationMins.description: The window's length in minutes; 300 is 5 hours.

resetsAt.description: When it resets, epoch ms; null when Codex didn't say.

fetchedAt.description: When it was read from Codex, epoch ms; cached up to 30 s.

tools.description: List closed agent sessions that can be relaunched, from the on-disk journal: which sessions exist, no transcript text. Needs a worktree or project scope and fails when none resolves. Old sessions are pruned, so absence proves nothing.

worktreeId.description: Only this worktree.

examples.description: List the most recent resumable sessions for one worktree
List up to 50 resumable sessions across one project

tools.description: Relaunch one closed agent session by exact id and return its pane. It relaunches in the worktree it was recorded in, so one recorded outside the named worktree is refused. A repeat call brings the live pane forward, not a second agent. Opens off-screen unless that worktree is active.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing. Omit it and the path for the active worktree; fails when none is active.

worktreePath.description: Absolute worktree root, instead of the id. The id wins if both; the path is never swapped for the active one.

sessionId.description: Exact session id from a session-history or bookmark listing; never a title or prefix.

examples.description: Resume one journaled session in the worktree it was recorded in

tools.description: List the other Daintree Assistants running in this project, and its vacant slots. Address one by its terminalId with the agent messaging tools; a send passes its generation.

terminalId.description: Its terminal: what a send, notice, read or close names.

generation.description: Its run's generation. A send passes it back; a restarted run has a new one.

agentState.description: As last observed; not proof of what it is doing.

tools.description: Open another Daintree Assistant in this project with no window, in a vacant slot, and return it as the assistant listing does. Not ready still means it runs; don't open another.

slot.description: A vacant slot. Omit for the lowest vacant one.

agentId.description: claude, codex or copilot. Omit for this machine's default.

terminalId.description: Its terminal: what a send, notice, read or close names.

generation.description: Its run's generation. A send passes it back; a restarted run has a new one.

agentState.description: As last observed; not proof of what it is doing.

ready.description: At its prompt. False: it runs but is stopped short of one; don't start another.

tools.description: Read captured console output (logs, warnings, errors, stack traces) from a dev preview panel: the newest messages plus error and warning counts.

limit.description: Max messages, newest first (max 500). Omit for all.

tools.description: Bundle a worktree's file tree and selected contents into a context file on disk and return its path; never inline, often tens of MB. To give an agent context, inject into its terminal instead. Check the budget flags before trusting it, and read it promptly: it is pruned by age.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing. Omit it and the path for the active worktree; fails when none is active.

worktreePath.description: Absolute worktree root, instead of the id. The id wins if both; the path is never swapped for the active one.

filter.description: Worktree-relative file paths or globs to include. Patterns match file paths, so a folder needs a glob: pass 'src/panels/**', not 'src/panels'; prefer `scopePaths` for a folder. Combined with `includePaths`; omit both for the whole worktree. An empty list or blank entry is rejected.

always.description: Force-include matches past ignore files, project and config exclusions, your `exclude`, the `modified`/`changed` filters and `maxFileSize`. Blunt: a broad pattern can pull in `node_modules`, and `../` reaches outside the worktree. It does not override `.git`, the 10MB memory ceiling, or the `maxFileCount`/`maxTotalSize`/`charLimit` budgets. To pass one ignore rule, use `scopePaths` with `scopeIgnoresIgnoreFiles`.

includePaths.description: Worktree-relative file paths or globs, for a curated bundle of scattered files (sources, supporting code, tests). Patterns match file paths, so a folder needs a glob: pass 'src/panels/**', not 'src/panels'; prefer `scopePaths` for a folder. Combined with `filter` when both are given. Unlike `scopePaths` it does not restrict traversal.

scopePaths.description: Subtrees to restrict the copy to, as worktree-relative literal file or directory paths, not glob patterns: pass 'src/panels', not 'src/panels/**'. Prefer this over `filter` or `includePaths` for a folder. An empty list is rejected rather than copying everything. Restricts traversal, so `filter` and `includePaths` can only narrow within it.

scopeIgnoresIgnoreFiles.description: Let `scopePaths` into subtrees a `.copytreeignore` or `.gitignore` rule would prune (default false). Requires `scopePaths`. Only the rules blocking entry into each scoped path are lifted; other rules, negations and nested ignore files all still apply, as do node_modules and config exclusions, `exclude`, `.git`, the git filters, `maxFileSize` and budgets. For a rule inside a selected folder, scope the exact file instead: a scoped folder subsumes its listed children.

maxFileSize.description: Per-file cap in bytes, positive. Omit for none.

maxTotalSize.description: Total bundle cap in bytes, positive. Omit for none.

maxFileCount.description: Max files included, positive. Omit for none.

charLimit.description: Character cap on the rendered bundle, positive. Omit for none.

name.description: 2-4 word label ('auth flow context') for the copy-tree history and notification.

includeContent.description: Also return a bounded head of the bundle in `content`; `contentTruncated` says if it was cut. The file always holds the whole bundle.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the written bundle. Temporary — read it promptly.

outputBytes.description: UTF-8 size of the bundle on disk.

outputFormatVersion.description: Version of the emitted format, e.g. `copytree-xml@1`.

content.description: Head of the bundle, only when `includeContent` was set.

estimatedTokens.description: Rough token count, accurate to about ±20%

noFilesMatched.description: Nothing matched — a valid outcome, not error

unmatchedSelector.description: Selector that matched no files. For a folder, add '/**' or use scopePaths.

truncated.description: A budget dropped or cut short some files

truncatedBy.description: Which budget bit first: maxFileCount, maxTotalSize or charLimit

budgetExceeded.description: The retained set is larger than maxTotalSize — can be true without truncation

tools.description: Reload the dev preview page without restarting its dev server. Try this first when the preview looks stale; restart the server only when its process is wedged or its config changed.
Stop the dev server and start it again, keeping caches and dependencies. The preview is down until it returns; reload the page first unless the server process itself is the problem.

Collect a diagnostics snapshot and open the review dialog, where the user picks sections and adds redaction rules before saving the export themselves. The way to hand logs to someone else: nothing leaves the machine from this call.

sections.description: Section keys to pre-select; every other section starts unchecked. Omit for all.

tools.description: List recent diagnostics error-log entries (runtime and inter-process failures), newest first. Separate from the notification inbox; read both for a full picture. Dismissed entries are omitted by default.

Read the fleet broadcast the user is running, with per-terminal delivery and liveness. Observe only: it dispatches nothing. Agent state here is a passive heuristic and a parsed check result is not an exit code; confirm both before acting.

Fetch the roll-up CI verdict for one pull request. Read the overall state: counts cover required checks only, and a zero total also appears when that list could not be read, so it never proves nothing gates the merge. Provider-cached; can lag a minute.

tools.description: Show a documentation image inline in the assistant panel, only when it genuinely illustrates the answer. Cite the returned figure label as plain text where it belongs, not as markdown image syntax, which CLI renderers strip. Never choose figure numbers yourself.

url.description: An https://daintree.org image URL. data:, blob:, and other hosts are rejected.

examples.description: A daintree-docs result returned this screenshot and it directly illustrates the answer — pin it, then write the returned `figureLabel` (e.g. `[image #N]`) at the relevant point in the reply.

tools.description: Run a host's own Daintree tool in one of its projects (local reaches another project here) and get its result, such as starting its assistant. Changes are refused while another machine drives that project. ambiguous: resend under its callId, which never runs twice.

hostId.description: A host id from the host list.

projectId.description: A projectId from the host list. The call runs there.

throwaway.description: Instead of projectId: a short-lived agent this session owns, in a host folder. Tools: throwaway.launch, status, output, sendCommand, sendKeys, close.

tool.description: A Daintree tool on the host, by id. Search the host's own tools through this.

callId.description: Resend an ambiguous call under its callId. It never runs twice.

newCallId.description: Your own fresh UUID for a write; with no answer back, resend under it as callId. Never both.

annotations.title: Run a tool on a host

tools.description: Make sure this project is on a host: its copy found, else cloned there, plus the branch's worktree when asked. Returns the host's projectId to run its tools in. Never pushes, opens a window or runs setup; choices for the person come back as questions. working: call again the same way.

hostId.description: A host id from the host list.

worktree.description: Also make the branch's worktree there, at the remote's commit.

worktreePath.description: Which of this project's worktrees has the branch. Default: the project folder.

copy.description: The person's answer to a copies question: a path it named, or "new" to clone.

accept.description: Questions the person agreed to go past, up to 2.

annotations.title: Bring this project to a host

tools.description: List the hosts this assistant reaches, this machine first as local, as observed: connection, load sample, agent counts and each connected host's projects, which calls name. Null means unmeasured.

includeAgents.description: Also list each host's agents: its workers and Daintree Assistants, as observed. Read the coverage before reading an empty list as nothing running.

projectId.description: With includeAgents, list only the agents of this project (a projectId from the list).

stale.description: Too old to trust: the live figures below are null. Not a zero reading.

cpuBusyCores.description: cpuPercent of the cores it is a share of: all logical cores, or a cgroup quota.

memoryAvailableBytes.description: Total minus used, as the host counts.

memoryCapacityReported.description: False: an older host whose used memory includes file cache, so none is given.

load.description: Null: no sample. Any null field inside is unknown, never zero or unlimited.

frontendAttached.description: A frontend is attached: a view there or a driving Shell. If false, only tools the host runs itself run. Null: unknown.

tools.description: Read or change named settings on hosts, such as turning Canopy on across several. preview returns a ticket and changes nothing; apply asks the person to approve exactly that preview, then writes it. Never this machine's own settings.

operation.description: read: current values. preview: what patch would change, and a ticket. apply: run it.

hostIds.description: For read and preview: the exact hosts, up to 8.

items.description: A host id from the host list.

keys.description: For read: which settings, up to 5. Default: all.

patch.description: For preview: values to set on every host named.

ticket.description: For apply: a preview's ticket. The person approves it in a dialog here first.

tools.description: Move this window to another Daintree host. No args opens the host palette; hostId ("local" or from the list) opens its last project here, else its project list.

hostId.description: A host id from the host list, or "local" for this machine.

newWindow.description: Open the host in a new window instead of switching this one.

tools.description: Report this session's tool surface as data: its tier, a stable hash, and per-tool tier, kind, read-only and idempotency hints and deprecation. Call once at startup to check it matches what this client expects, then compare the hash to detect drift.

manifestVersion.description: Payload shape version, bumped when a field changes meaning

tier.description: The authorization tier this call was admitted at

hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of the surface, for drift checks

tier.description: Lowest tier on this caller's ladder that permits the tool

readOnlyHint.description: The tool does not modify state, so a retry is safe

idempotentHint.description: Repeating with the same arguments has no further effect

deprecated.description: Present only when the tool is on its way out

tools.description: Every tool `tools/list` advertises here, sorted by id

List recent notification-inbox entries (completion, waiting and info messages, including quiet ones never toasted), newest first. Separate from the diagnostics error log; read both for a full picture. Never fails.

unreadOnly.description: Only ones not yet seen as a toast (default false)

tools.description: A PNG of one plugin panel as it renders, plus the plugin's recent console warnings and errors. Refused with no image while the panel is hidden, off screen or covered by a dialog, menu or tooltip.

panelId.description: The plugin panel to capture; focus is never assumed.

tools.description: Report why a plugin is in its state: its recorded load or activation failure, whether it runs, and its recent host-logger lines. A refused project plugin is reported with its rejection. An unknown id fails, listing the ids that exist.

pluginId.description: Manifest id, publisher.name. For a project plugin, the manifest id, not its directory.

logLimit.description: Newest log lines to return (default 50, max 500).

examples.description: Find out why a plugin that should be running isn't.
Pull a deeper log tail while chasing an intermittent activation failure.

tools.description: Remount a plugin panel's view, keeping its backend and persisted state; unpersisted view state is lost. A view reporting unsaved work is left alone, a confirmation is staged for the user, and the call fails.

panelId.description: The plugin panel to reload; focus is never assumed.

tools.description: Re-scan the open project's committed plugins, reconcile what runs with what is on disk, and report every plugin directory found. Picks up a new or rebuilt plugin without reopening the project. Trust rules still apply: an id the project never ran is listed, not executed.

Check a plugin.json on disk against the schema Daintree loads with, returning each rejection with its field path. Rules differ by plugin location; the reply names the rule set applied and why. Warnings never stop loading.

path.description: Plugin directory or manifest file, absolute or project-relative, inside the open project or the managed plugins directory.

examples.description: Check a project plugin the agent just wrote, before reloading.
The same check, naming the manifest file directly.

tools.description: Detect the runnable commands a project defines from its manifest files, instead of guessing. Returns every script, publish and deploy included, and synthesizes conventional ones for some frameworks; check what a command does before running it.
Open this project on another host via git: finds the host's copy by remote URL or clones it, then offers a worktree. Opens a dialog that confirms every step.

hostId.description: A host id from the host list, or "local" for this machine.

projectId.description: The project to open, as this window knows it.

newWindow.description: Open the project on the host in a new window instead of this one.

worktree.description: Create this worktree on the host once the project is there, instead of handing over the current branch.

relativePath.description: Where the worktree goes, relative to the project folder; null for the host's pattern.

navigateOnly.description: Open the host's copy as is, branch untouched.

tools.description: Run one detected project command and report its exit code and output. A failing command is a failed check, not an error, so read the result. Detection lists every script, not just checks: verify an unfamiliar one first. Never for long-lived servers; they block until timeout.

projectId.description: Project id from the project listing.

runnerId.description: Runner id from detection; confirm what an unfamiliar id runs first.

cwd.description: The project root or one of its worktrees (default: project root).

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock ceiling in ms (default 600000, min 1000, max 3600000); the process tree is killed at expiry.

tools.description: Run one non-interactive shell command on this host and return its exit code, output and timing. cwd is where it starts, not a sandbox: it runs as the host's user. A non-zero exit is a result, not an error. Never for servers or prompts.

projectId.description: Project id from the project listing.

command.description: Shell command line, run as given, with no stdin or TTY.

cwd.description: Project root or one of its worktrees (default: root).

timeoutMs.description: Ms before the process tree is killed (default 600000).

tools.description: List the project's saved recipes, named multi-terminal setups from the user or plugins, each with its origin, to find recipe ids. Never fails; an empty list while still loading means not read yet, not none.

worktreeId.description: Only recipes available in this worktree. Omit for every recipe in the project.

tools.description: Launch the terminals a saved recipe defines in one worktree, starting their commands or agents. For a single pane, launch an agent or terminal instead. An approved call starts every terminal, a pre-authorized one at most three, so check what started.

recipeId.description: Recipe id from the recipe listing; an unknown id fails before any terminal starts.

worktreeId.description: Worktree for the recipe's terminals (default: active worktree).

spawnedBy.description: Run-history provenance only. Leave unset over MCP.

focusPolicy.description: Focus the new panel: "auto" (default) unless the assistant owns input, "preserve" never, "take" always. Use preserve for background spawns.

spawnedTerminalIds.description: Panels this run started, in spawn order.

tools.description: Read the full instructions of one plugin-contributed skill, to follow in the current task. Get the id from a skills search; ids are plugin-namespaced and not guessable. An unknown id fails.

id.description: Skill id from a skills search.

tools.description: Find plugin-contributed skills: reusable instructions and workflows, such as a review rubric or a TDD procedure. Returns names and summaries only; load one by id to read it. Without a query it lists skills up to the limit, never saying if more exist.

query.description: Keywords. Omit or empty to list unfiltered, still bounded by the limit.

tools.description: List the slash commands an agent CLI offers, including project-local ones, before driving the agent with one. An empty list means it has none.

projectId.description: Project id from the project listing. Omit it and the path for the active project; an unknown id is rejected, not retargeted, once open projects are known.

projectPath.description: Absolute project root, instead of the id. The id wins if both.

agentId.description: Agent ID. Defaults to 'claude' when omitted.

tools.description: Close a terminal or any other panel, usually to the trash, where it stays briefly recoverable; remove-on-exit and dialog panels are discarded outright. Name the panel: the wrong one discards someone's work. An untracked panel is rejected; the result names what closed.

terminalId.description: Panel `id` from the terminal listing. Automated callers must pass it; omitted, the focused panel closes.

closedIds.description: Panels closed. Empty means nothing closed (none to act on, already in the trash, or teardown failed): treat it as a failed close.

tools.description: Close every panel in the active worktree, not just terminals, including the user's shells and other agents' terminals; prefer closing individually. Most go to the trash; remove-on-exit panels are discarded. Internal and dialog panels are spared.

closedIds.description: Panels closed. Empty means nothing closed (none to act on, already in the trash, or teardown failed): treat it as a failed close.

tools.description: Close several terminals in one call, each as a single close (owned for an agent pane), to the trash. Results come back in order.

terminalIds.description: 1-16 terminals to close, each as a single close.

tools.description: Read one terminal's trailing output: what an agent or command printed. For several, the status snapshot reads every tail in one call. ANSI is stripped by default; a missing terminal returns an error field, not a failed call.

terminalId.description: Panel id from the terminal listing. An untracked id returns an error field, not a failed call.

truncated.description: True when older output was left out, by `maxLines` or the 50 KiB response budget; the newest lines are kept.

examples.description: Get last 100 lines from a terminal with ANSI stripped
Get last 500 lines with ANSI codes preserved

tools.description: Snapshot agent and process state for many terminals in one call, with optional output tails, and confirm a submission landed. Prefer it to listing terminals or reading each. Never fails whole; an entry's error means that terminal was missing or unreadable.

terminalIds.description: 1-256 terminals; overrides the filters. An unknown id gets an `error` entry, not a failed call.

worktreeId.description: Filter by worktree.

location.description: Filter by location. Default: all but trash and background.

submissionToken.description: Token from a send; adds its delivery record to each entry. Needs `terminalIds`.

includeOutput.description: `true` or options: adds `recentOutput` (last N lines), plus `lastOutputChangeAt` and `lastTypedInputAt` when observed.

lastOutputChangeAt.description: Epoch ms the screen last changed, ignoring spinner and timer redraws. Absent if unobserved. Not a hang verdict.

lastTypedInputAt.description: Epoch ms of last PTY input (keys, paste, broadcast, withdrawn sends). Before `lastTransitionAt` means none since. Not proof of delivery or authorship.

exitCode.description: Set once the process exits, so absence means still running unless listed in `unavailableFields`. Null means killed by a signal with no numeric code.

agentIncarnation.description: Times a new agent took over this PTY after one exited, which `spawnedAt` misses. Absent is unobserved, not 0.

lastCheckResult.description: Best-effort parse of the agent's latest test, lint or build summary from its output, not an exit code. Absence means no summary seen, not no check and not a pass. Check its time for freshness.

lastHandback.description: The handback marker the agent printed: an observation, not a finish verdict; `message` is its own untrusted summary. Absence never means still working.

message.description: Rows rejoined, so lossy. Null for a bare marker. Read the last message for exact text.

recentOutputTruncated.description: Older output was cut, by `lines` or the shared 50 KiB budget; the newest lines are kept.

armed.description: Whether fleet broadcast input reaches this terminal. Set for every found terminal unless in `unavailableFields`.

hasPty.description: False once the process exited or a kill was requested. Not a health probe: a keep-open shell or a wedged agent still reads true. Unavailable on the `renderer` surface.

submission.description: Delivery record for the named token. Absent without a token or when the terminal could not be read, which differs from holding no record.

phase.description: `pty_written`: the text and its Enter reached the pty; it does NOT mean the agent read or acted on them. `queued`/`writing`: in progress. `failed`/`cancelled`: not sent whole and part may sit in the composer, so re-sending is not safe. `unknown`: no record, including tokens older than the last 32.

at.description: Epoch ms the phase was entered. Absent for `unknown`.

outputChangeAfterWriteAt.description: For pty_written only: epoch ms of the latest screen change stamped >200ms after the Enter. Ordering, not attribution; absent means no such change seen.

error.description: Set when the terminal was not found, and on every resolved entry when a batched fetch fails; then the status fields are still set and only that fetch's field is missing. Never fails the call.

source.description: Which surface answered; `pty` is the reduced reading when this workspace has no open window.

unavailableFields.description: Fields this surface cannot observe: absent from every entry, unknown rather than false.

tools.description: Write the active worktree's prepared context into a terminal, to hand an agent a large codebase context. Name the target: focus can drift, and a mistarget types a large dump into the wrong pane. Target an idle terminal.

terminalId.description: Terminal to inject into. Automated callers must name it; focus can drift.

tools.description: Interrupt the turn an agent is running in a panel this connection created or was handed (right-click > Hand to orchestrator), keeping the panel and conversation. Sends cancel keystrokes, not prompt text. An idle agent, or one binding a different cancel key, is refused rather than reported stopped. Read the terminal for the effect.

terminalId.description: Agent panel `id` this session created or was handed. Required; no focus fallback.
The panel the cancel keystrokes were addressed to.

agentId.description: The agent Daintree resolved for that panel, from its runtime identity.

agentStateAtDispatch.description: Last observed agent state, read off its output and often wrong; it gated the request, not proof a turn was running.

status.description: `requested`: keystrokes handed to an agent whose CLI names Escape as its interrupt. `requested-unverified`: that CLI names no interrupt key. Neither says the keystrokes arrived or the agent stopped; read the terminal's output.

tools.description: Permanently destroy a panel of any kind and its process: no trash, no recovery. A panel running an agent session is left alone unless confirmed, and the call then fails. Name the panel explicitly; close it instead when recovery matters.

confirmed.description: Confirms losing a running agent session; redundant once the host prompted. Otherwise the panel is left alone, a confirmation is staged and the call fails.

tools.description: List open terminals and panels with enough metadata to pick one and learn its id. A cheap inventory, not a polling path: the status snapshot carries agent state for many in one call. Ephemeral and internal panels are omitted; empty means nothing matched.

worktreeId.description: Only this worktree. Omit for every worktree in the project.

location.description: Only this location. Omitted, trash and background are excluded.

owned.description: MCP only: true keeps only terminals you created or were handed; false or omitted, no filter. An agent pane keeps them across reconnects.

terminalId.description: Only this panel id; one not open yields an empty listing, not an error.

includeClientMetadata.description: Add each terminal's client-metadata record (up to 2KB each); narrow the listing on a large fleet.

restored.description: Set when restore rebuilt the pane (`at`, epoch ms). lastSeen: agent state saved before then, not proof a run ended.

tools.description: Move a terminal panel to another worktree, reversibly. The process is never restarted: a live agent keeps running in its launch directory, and its pane offers to tell it to continue there. Panels in the same tab group move too. Name the target; an automated caller cannot see focus.

Open a new terminal shell, ready for commands; it uses resources until closed. Defaults to the active worktree, or opens at a chosen directory and runs a command there. To start an AI CLI, launch an agent instead.

spawnedBy.description: Run-history provenance only. Leave unset over MCP.

focusPolicy.description: Focus the new panel: "auto" (default) unless the assistant owns input, "preserve" never, "take" always. Use preserve for background spawns.

cwd.description: Absolute directory (default: active worktree root). Requires a confirmation.

command.description: Shell command to run at once instead of leaving a prompt. Requires a confirmation.

tools.description: Be told when a working agent terminal stops, instead of polling. Returns at once; when it next stops working, Daintree types what it saw, your note and its last screen lines into your prompt. End your turn after calling. A terminal not working comes back unarmed. When sending a prompt, set notify on the send instead.

terminalId.description: A working agent terminal in your project, not your own.

note.description: Echoed in the notice, e.g. the next step. One line, at most 160 characters.

replyLines.description: With notify: screen lines quoted (default 40, 0 for none); with handback, up to the marker. Set, it quotes despite a summary.

armed.description: False when the terminal was not working: nothing was set up, and `state` is where it is now.

tools.description: Move a panel this session created or was handed to the background, dock or grid; its process keeps running. Never takes focus or moves the user. Other panels are refused.

terminalId.description: Panel `id` this session created or was handed.

location.description: Where the panel is now. Null means nothing was targeted (no panel named and none focused).

tools.description: Read an agent's last transcript reply and unanswered tool calls, e.g. a question and its options. Agents this connection launched or was handed (right-click > Hand to orchestrator); Daintree's assistant: any in its project. Claude Code only, or another assistant's screen. Not proof the agent is waiting.

terminalId.description: Agent panel `id` the description says you may read. Required; no focus fallback.

maxBytes.description: Text budget in escaped bytes, 1024 to 49152; default 24576.

messageIndex.description: Replies back from the latest with text: 0 (default) to 20. Not with `cursor`.

cursor.description: A result's `message.nextCursor`, unchanged, for the text before that page.

text.description: Its text blocks in order, cut to `maxBytes` once escaped, keeping the end.

truncated.description: The start of the message was cut to fit.

stopReason.description: Raw from the transcript, not a verdict on whether the turn ended.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the text before this. Null once nothing earlier is in reach.

message.description: The selected reply with text. Null when only an unanswered tool call is on record.

input.description: Only on a question to the user; omitted whole when too large or deep.

unansweredToolUses.description: Calls in or after the message with no later result, oldest first, at most 8. Not proof the agent is waiting on one.

newerRecordsFollow.description: A prompt, tool result or later message follows the text, or a line is still being written.

reason.description: 'provider-mismatch': an agent this cannot read. 'store-unknown': the pane's store is uncertain; nothing read. 'search-cap-reached': no reply within the bounded read; no older one substituted. 'message-not-found': no reply at that index, or the cursor's message changed.

source.description: Another assistant's screen, to its handback or before one.

examples.description: An agent you launched stopped, and you need its hand-off or the exact question it asked before replying.

tools.description: Set a terminal tab's title, or clear it to the default. Pass the terminal and the title: an omitted title opens a dialog an automated caller cannot answer. Returns the title now shown; `applied` is false when a title the user set by hand kept its place.

name.description: New title; omitted, opens the rename dialog.

tools.description: Restart a terminal's process in place, keeping the pane. Returns before the restart finishes; watch its status before sending. A running agent session is left alone unless confirmed; otherwise whatever ran is killed and unsaved state lost. A panel with no process is ignored.

confirmed.description: Confirms interrupting a running agent session; redundant once the host prompted. Otherwise the terminal is untouched, a confirm is staged and the call fails.

tools.description: Respawn an agent panel this session launched on another preset of its agent, in place, after the user confirms: for an agent that hit a plan limit. Its conversation and scrollback are lost. Panels it was handed are refused.

terminalId.description: Panel `id` this session got when launching it. Required.

presetId.description: A preset `id` of the panel's own agent.

agentSessionIdCleared.description: A new conversation started: re-send anything the agent still needs.

annotations.title: Move owned agent to another preset

tools.description: Bring the user to a panel this session created or was handed (right-click > Hand to orchestrator), switching workspace and raising the window if needed. No other panel can be revealed. Use it when the user asked to be taken there, not to report progress.

terminalId.description: Panel `id` this session created or was handed.

tools.description: Queue text as one submission to a terminal: a shell runs it, an agent pane takes it as its next prompt. Returns once queued, not delivered or run; pass the returned `submissionToken` to a status read to check. Runs with the terminal's privileges.

terminalId.description: Panel id from the terminal listing.

command.description: A shell command or the agent's next prompt. Multi-line text goes in atomically with one Enter.

handback.description: Ask the agent to end its reply with a Daintree marker, read back as `lastHandback`. Agent panes only.

generation.description: Sending to another assistant: its generation from the assistant listing.

notify.description: When this agent next stops, Daintree types its handback summary, else its screen, into your prompt; may be missed: poll too. Agent panes and assistants only.

replyLines.description: With notify: screen lines quoted (default 40, 0 for none); with handback, up to the marker. Set, it quotes despite a summary.

waitForReply.description: Hold the call until the agent finishes; its reply comes back in `reply`.

sent.description: Accepted onto the terminal's lane; not evidence of delivery.

command.description: The submitted text, cut past 1024 characters: an echo, not a receipt.

submissionToken.description: Pass with `terminalId` to a status read to see how far it got. Kept for the last 32 per terminal; lost on restart.

tools.description: Submit a different message to each of several terminals in one call, such as one ballot per voter. Each runs as a single send, with its own notice; results come back in order.

sends.description: 1-16 messages, one per terminal, each its next prompt.

notify.description: As on a single call: each notice carries that agent's reply.

handback.description: As on the single call, for each item.

replyLines.description: With notify: screen lines quoted (default 40, 0 for none); with handback, up to the marker. Set, it quotes despite a summary.

waitForReply.description: Hold the call until every agent finishes; each result has its `reply`.

tools.description: Answer a CLI's own dialog in a terminal (trust, permission, a list) by option label or named keys. A send can't: it types text then Enter, taking whatever is highlighted.

terminalId.description: The terminal to press keys in.

choose.description: An option's label as shown; Daintree moves to it and presses Enter. Prefer it to `keys`.

keys.description: Or up to 16 of: Up, Down, Left, Right, Enter, Escape, Tab, Space, Backspace, a-z, 0-9.

notify.description: As on a send: hear, with its reply, when the turn these keys unblock ends.

replyLines.description: With notify: screen lines quoted (default 40, 0 for none); with handback, up to the marker. Set, it quotes despite a summary.

tools.description: Attach your own JSON record to a terminal so a reconnecting client can tell panels apart. It outlives your connection and restarts, and dies with the panel; read it back from the terminal listing, null clears it. Shared: every external client sees the same record, and it confers no ownership.

terminalId.description: Panel id from the terminal listing.

clientMetadata.description: Replaces the whole record, not a patch. Max 2048 bytes of JSON, 16 deep; null deletes it. Namespace your keys: it is shared.

examples.description: Record which of your logical sessions a terminal belongs to
Clear the record you stored against a terminal

tools.description: Block until the agent in one terminal stops working. For several, use the batched wait; to poll without blocking, a status snapshot. A timeout is normal and means still working. A closed terminal also reads as idle, so check `trackingState`.

terminalId.description: Panel id from the terminal listing. A closed or unknown id resolves as idle, not a failure.

timeoutMs.description: 0 for an immediate snapshot (recommended); otherwise max ms to long-poll, default 60s. Interactive sessions cap at 60s, headless at 2 hours.

idleReason.description: 'idle' at rest, 'waiting_for_user' blocked on input, 'completed' or 'exited' once ended, 'unknown' untracked. Only the ended states carry an exit code.

trackingState.description: 'tracked': a mapping is held, not proof of liveness or completion; 'closed': a kill was observed; 'unknown': no record (a plain shell, a poll racing the spawn, or evicted history).

waitingReason.description: Only when idleReason is 'waiting_for_user'. 'prompt': empty input prompt, or the fallback when nothing else matched; confirm before driving. 'question': the agent asks the user. 'approval': a permission selector needs a choice. 'error': stopped on a blocking error (auth, rate limit, network, failed command).

lastOutputChangeAt.description: Epoch ms the screen last changed, ignoring spinner and timer redraws. Absent if unobserved. Not a hang verdict.

lastHandback.description: The handback marker the agent printed: an observation, not a finish verdict; `message` is its own untrusted summary. Absence never means still working.

exitCode.description: Only when idleReason is 'completed' or 'exited'. null = signal-terminated with no numeric code.

exitSignal.description: Terminating OS signal number, once ended.

timedOut.description: The wait elapsed with the agent still working. Call again; not a failure.

tools.description: Block until the first of several agents stops working, or all of them do: the fan-out wait when agents finish at different speeds. A timeout means not met yet. A gone terminal settles too, so read `trackingState`.

terminalIds.description: Terminals to watch, 1-256. Closed or unknown ids settle rather than fail; each row's `trackingState` says which.

mode.description: 'first' returns when any one stops (refill as each frees up), 'all' once every one has (a join).

timeoutMs.description: 0 for an immediate snapshot; otherwise max ms to long-poll, default 60s. Interactive sessions cap at 60s, headless at 2 hours.

trackingState.description: 'tracked': a mapping is held, not proof of liveness or completion; 'closed': a kill was observed; 'unknown': no record (a plain shell, a poll racing the spawn, or evicted history).

lastOutputChangeAt.description: Epoch ms the screen last changed, ignoring spinner and timer redraws. Absent if unobserved. Not a hang verdict.

lastHandback.description: The handback marker the agent printed: an observation, not a finish verdict; `message` is its own untrusted summary. Absence never means still working.

settled.description: This row satisfied the wait. Gone terminals settle too, which is not completion; read trackingState.

tools.description: Inspect a worktree and report go/no-go on starting review checks, naming blockers. Read-only despite the name: it prepares and runs nothing. Use it to avoid running checks on a dirty or conflicted tree.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing. Omit it and the path for the active worktree; fails when none is active.

worktreePath.description: Absolute worktree root, instead of the id. The id wins if both; the path is never swapped for the active one.

projectId.description: Project for runner detection (default: current). Pass it when the worktree belongs to another project.

tools.description: Start work on an issue in one call: fetch it, create a worktree on a derived branch, launch an agent in a terminal and inject context. An unknown or non-terminal agent id is rejected before the issue lookup, so no worktree is created.

issueNumber.description: Issue number to start work on

agentId.description: Agent CLI to launch, e.g. 'claude' or 'codex'; 'terminal' for a plain shell. Ids from the agent listing; an unknown one is rejected before anything is created.

branchName.description: Defaults to 'feature/issue-<number>-<slug>' from the issue title.

baseBranch.description: Base branch (default: the main worktree's branch)

recipeId.description: Recipe ID to run after creation

assignToSelf.description: Assign the issue to the current user. Omit for the saved 'Assign issue to me' preference.

injectContext.description: Inject worktree context into the terminal (default true)

spawnedBy.description: Run-history provenance only. Leave unset over MCP.

focusPolicy.description: Focus the new panel: "auto" (default) unless the assistant owns input, "preserve" never, "take" always. Use preserve for background spawns.

tools.description: List every project and scratch workspace Daintree knows, open or not, to look up a workspace id instead of hashing a path. workspaceId is what the Daintree-Workspace-Id header binds to. hasLiveView says a view is open; only absence from this list makes an id wrong.

frontendAttached.description: A frontend is attached: a view here or a driving Shell. If false, only tools the host runs itself run. Null: unknown.

tools.description: Create a managed git worktree; Daintree's creator also copies project config, initializes submodules and runs setup. Pick one mode: new branch, existing branch as named, or pull request. A recipe is optional, only to launch terminals. Setup runs in the background and can fail after this returns.

kind.description: Branch off a base branch; a taken name follows `collisionPolicy`.

branchName.description: New branch name; an invalid git ref is rejected, not rewritten.

baseBranch.description: Base branch (default: the main worktree's branch).

fromRemote.description: Set true if baseBranch names a remote branch, e.g. origin/develop.

collisionPolicy.description: If the name is taken: 'suffix' (default) reuses the branch when nothing has it checked out, else creates name-2, and reports which; 'error' fails.

issueNumber.description: Issue this worktree is for, passed to the recipe and assignToSelf; it does not attach the issue.

assignToSelf.description: Assign the linked issue to the current user. Omit for the saved 'Assign issue to me' preference.

kind.description: Check out an existing local branch exactly as named.

branchName.description: Existing local branch, used verbatim: never suffixed, never replaced by a new branch if missing.

issueNumber.description: Issue this worktree is for, passed to the recipe and assignToSelf; it does not attach the issue.

assignToSelf.description: Assign the linked issue to the current user. Omit for the saved 'Assign issue to me' preference.

kind.description: Check out a pull request's head branch. State is unchecked: a closed or merged PR works while its head ref exists.

pullRequestNumber.description: Pull request to check out; its head branch is fetched for you, so pass no branch name.

source.description: Where the branch comes from; exactly one mode.

recipeId.description: Recipe to launch in the new worktree. Omit for no terminals; setup starts either way and terminals do not wait for it.

spawnedBy.description: Run-history provenance only. Leave unset over MCP.

focusPolicy.description: Focus the new panel: "auto" (default) unless the assistant owns input, "preserve" never, "take" always. Use preserve for background spawns.

tools.description: Delete a linked worktree and its directory. Refuses uncommitted or untracked changes unless forced, which destroys them irreversibly. The main worktree cannot be deleted. Commit or push anything worth keeping first.

Delete a worktree this session created, removing its directory after the user confirms. Anything else is refused. It never forces past uncommitted or untracked changes, deletes the branch, or closes terminals it does not own; commit or close those first.

worktreeId.description: The `worktreeId` this session got when creating the worktree.

tools.description: Get the worktree in use, which most work should be scoped to. An empty result means none is active or it can no longer be found; handle that before acting.
List every worktree in the active project with its branch, status and linked issue or pull request, to discover worktree ids. Never fails; empty means the project has none.

Run the project's pause commands for a worktree's remote resource, typically stopping a cloud devbox to save cost. These are arbitrary project commands; resume is a separate sequence, not guaranteed to undo this.

Run the project's provisioning commands for a worktree's remote resource, such as creating a cloud devbox. Creates real infrastructure and may cost money; teardown is separate. Confirm the target worktree first.
Run the project's resume commands to bring a paused remote resource back up. May take time and cost money once it returns; on a resource never paused it does whatever the command does.

Run the project's status command for a worktree's remote resource, such as a cloud devbox, and report its output. Runs a real command and waits. Reports nothing when none is configured; a failing command fails the call rather than returning a cached answer.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing (default: focused or active worktree).

tools.description: Run the project's teardown commands for a worktree's remote resource, typically destroying a cloud devbox. What is destroyed and whether it is recoverable depends on that config; read it first. Pause is the lighter path if the resource is still needed.

Judge whether a worktree is ready to commit, push and merge, listing what blocks it. Read-only. Signals needing forge data that has not arrived report unknown, not passing; never read unknown as green.
Switch the active worktree, moving what the user sees and the default target of every later call that omits a worktree. Switching mid-task can silently retarget later work.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing.

tools.description: Names a worktree with a custom title shown in place of its issue, PR or branch headline on its card and in pickers. The computed headline stays visible beneath it. Cosmetic only.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id, from the worktree list

title.description: Custom title, at most 80 characters after whitespace is collapsed; null or blank clears it

tools.description: Marks a worktree with a colour on its sidebar card so the user can pick it out. The same colour replaces its automatic one in panel headers and pickers. Cosmetic only.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id, from the worktree list

tools.description: Wait until any given worktree has a detected pull request. Detection is a cached background poll: a PR seen, not opened, and not proof its agent finished. Returns at once if already detected. A timeout is not a failure; call again without the matched worktrees.

timeoutMs.description: Milliseconds to wait; 0 reads now. Default and max 25000.

worktrees.description: One per requested worktree, in order; PR fields null until detected.

timedOut.description: True if no PR was detected in time. Detection pauses while the project is backgrounded.

tools.description: Wait for a worktree's post-create setup (config copy, submodules, setup script, provisioning, plugin steps) and report where it got. Setup can outlive creation, so earlier work may see an unpopulated tree. A zero timeout reads without blocking; timing out is not a failure.

worktreeId.description: Worktree id from the worktree listing. Omit it and the path for the active worktree; fails when none is active.

worktreePath.description: Absolute worktree root, instead of the id. The id wins if both; the path is never swapped for the active one.

timeoutMs.description: Ms to wait; 0 reads now. Default and max 25000. Setup often runs longer: call again.

setupState.description: pending, running (config copy, submodules, setup script, provisioning, plugin steps), ready, failed, timed-out, needs-approval (awaits the user's approval; you can't give it), or unknown (not created by this host, or it restarted since).

stage.description: Stage running or failed; null before setup starts and once ready or unknown.

error.description: One-line failure summary when the state is failed or timed-out.

timedOut.description: The wait ran out before setup settled. The state is live; call again to keep waiting.
